clue.text: Terminated facility to enter data store

indicators.note: to enter says the word for facility goes inside the abbreviation for the data store

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, stores data
facility in the sense of ease, doing something without effort

explanation.surface: Some computing service has been shut down because it was allowed into a database.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that has stopped or come to an end.

clue.text: High point at one live broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread about

explanation.surface: A climax arrives at one point in a live transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is height above sea level, so a high place or hill.

clue.text: Calm witness takes in court briefly

indicators.note: takes in means the word for witness surrounds the shortened word

parts.note: to witness is to see

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A composed witness takes in proceedings in court for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means composed and unhurried, so tranquil.

clue.text: Devastating shot posing naked yields

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so these letters are rearranged
naked means stripped of the outer letters of yields

explanation.surface: A shot of someone posing nude brings results.
explanation.walkthrough: YIELDS stripped bare gives IELD, mixed with POSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Despoiling means plundering or laying waste, which is ravaging.

clue.text: Assumes arrest protects lives? Just the reverse!

indicators.note: Just the reverse tells us to read the whole assembled result backwards
protects means the word for arrest wraps round the word for lives

parts.note: to arrest is to stop
lives as in exists, IS

explanation.surface: An observation about policing: arresting people keeps them alive, or perhaps the opposite is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse!' sounds like a retort to the claim about policing, but it simply tells you to read the container, built with 'protects', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit something is to put it forward as a premise, taking it for granted.

clue.text: Vegetable matter burnt in the end

definitions.text: Vegetable matter burnt in the end

parts.words: Vegetable matter burnt in the end
parts.note: decayed plants pile up in bogs over centuries and are finally cut and dried as fuel for fires

explanation.surface: Kitchen vegetables that eventually got scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is partly decayed plant material from bogs, traditionally used as fuel.

clue.text: Cliff accepts my arrogant claim for weapon

indicators.note: accepts means the cliff word takes the claim inside it

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff
someone boasting says I'm it, I'm the one

explanation.surface: A clifftop boast that someone has a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAR, a northern English word for a crag, holds IMIT, the boast "I'm it".
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved sword of Middle Eastern origin.

clue.text: Joint of meat that's slightly off

indicators.note: slightly means only a small piece, the opening letter of the word

parts.note: game or meat that is going off is high

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut that has started to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper leg of a chicken is sold as a cut, and is also a body joint.

clue.text: Escort lame duck

indicators.note: lame means crippled, so the letters of Escort are reworked

explanation.surface: A man accompanies an injured duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lame duck' reads as one phrase, but 'duck' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck.

clue.text: Cell's nucleus missing from elementary component

indicators.note: nucleus missing from means the central letter of the particle word is removed

parts.note: a neutron is an elementary particle, a component of the atom

explanation.surface: A biology note: the cell's core is absent from a basic building block.
explanation.walkthrough: The nucleus of NEUTRON is its middle letter, T. The surface's biological nucleus is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell.

clue.text: Principles safeguarded by mediocre education

indicators.note: safeguarded by says the answer is kept within the following words

explanation.surface: A complaint that values are only protected by a second-rate schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs or guiding tenets.

clue.text: One lies drunk following attempt to get on an even keel

indicators.note: following places the earlier pieces after the word for attempt

parts.note: a stab is an attempt, as in have a stab at
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of lies are reeling about

explanation.surface: A drunk lies about steadying himself after a failed try at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the person in the picture; it is the anagram signal for 'lies' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To steady something is to make it balanced, the nautical idiom for which is an even keel.

clue.text: Drawing in pamphlet about gaining independence

indicators.note: gaining says the word for about acquires the independence letter at its front

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious
I is the usual abbreviation for independence or independent
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A leaflet on a country's struggle for self-rule is being drawn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the act of pulling or hauling a load.

clue.text: Internet Protocol they exposed in kernel of secret code

indicators.note: in puts the protocol letters and the stripped pronoun inside the core of the next word
kernel of means the middle letters of the word secret
exposed means the word they is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Computer people have revealed a networking protocol lurking at the heart of a hidden program.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of SECRET is CR; the middle of THEY is HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a system for disguising messages, a secret writing scheme.

clue.text: Setter could have prepared this mess

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, so its meal is what one might serve; the crossword setter is the misdirection

explanation.surface: The puzzle's setter admits to producing this muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's dinner is British slang for a muddled, badly done job.

clue.text: Bird's footprints not close to nest

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: a trail of footprints shows where an animal has gone

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of nest

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes tracks that stop short of the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail is a marsh bird, a relative of the coot and moorhen.

clue.text: Allotment using borders of agricultural site

indicators.note: borders of means the first and last letters of agricultural

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: A garden plot made by using the edges of farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment and an allocation are both a portion assigned or shared out.

clue.text: Critical MP being replaced by Tory leader bears repeating

indicators.note: being replaced by means the two letters are swapped for another

parts.note: imperative means vital, critical

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A political story: a critical MP being swapped for the Conservative chief is worth saying twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In IMPERATIVE the MP becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iterative involves repetition, done again and again.

clue.text: Stock trader ultimately assuming publicity will prop up market position

indicators.note: in a down answer, will prop up puts this piece below the next

parts.note: a stand is a stall at a market

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the trader's last letter is taken into the publicity word

parts.note: an ad is publicity

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of trader

explanation.surface: A financial tip: a dealer with publicity will support his position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like the financial noun, but it is the adjective meaning usual. In a down answer 'will prop up' puts the trader-and-publicity piece beneath the stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock and standard both mean usual or regular, as in a stock response.

clue.text: Able to take in damaged sense's limiting condition

indicators.note: damaged says all these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: fit means able, as in fit to work

explanation.surface: Someone capable of absorbing an impaired sense of things meets their limit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole pool FIT + IN + SENSE is rearranged; 'to take' links the able one to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bounded or having limits is the state of being finite.

clue.text: Foist Foreign Office onto expert that's not elected

indicators.note: onto places the abbreviation above the following word in this down entry
not means the letters for elected are left out

parts.note: a boffin is a scientific expert
in means elected, as a party is in power

explanation.surface: Diplomats impose upon an unelected specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: To fob someone off is to palm off something unwanted on them.

clue.text: Rich and famous wanting French author to return tax

indicators.note: to return means the remaining letters are read backwards
wanting means lacking, so the French word is taken away

parts.note: the jet set are the wealthy, glamorous people
the author of a clue refers to himself as I, which in French is je

explanation.surface: Celebrities without a French writer come back to be taxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the clue's author, 'I', and in French that is je. 'to return' reads what remains backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to test or strain them, as in a taxing problem.

clue.text: Move with little assurance right after support almost doubled

indicators.note: after places the right letter at the end
almost means the final letter is removed
doubled means the support word is written twice

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Advice to a nervous golfer: shift timidly, right, once the ball's on the peg.
explanation.walkthrough: TEE twice is TEETEE; 'almost' trims the last E.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble or move unsteadily.

clue.text: Crime having no lead or motive

indicators.note: having no lead means losing the first letter

parts.note: treason is a crime against the state

explanation.surface: A detective's problem: an offence without any clue or motive.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason for doing something is what drives it.

clue.text: Cold can drunk by giant

indicators.note: drunk by says the can is swallowed, taken inside the word for giant

parts.note: giant means big
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A huge man knocks back a beer can in the chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting wind is a sharply cold one.

clue.text: Short contribution to poster session

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brief presentation at an academic conference's display session.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief or curt in speech.

clue.text: Dead pianist's about to be replaced by tenor for free

indicators.note: to be replaced by swaps one letter of the name for another

parts.note: Liberace was a flamboyant American pianist who died in 1987
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A late pianist's role is about to pass to a singer, for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In LIBERACE the C becomes a T.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set at liberty, so a verb meaning release.

clue.text: Storyteller needing money to change hands

indicators.note: the left and right letters, L and R, swap places

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran

explanation.surface: A narrator needs cash to pass between people.
explanation.walkthrough: In RIAL, R (right) and L (left) swap, the hands changing.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar tells stories in the sense of fibs.

clue.text: Institution's behaviour helping head to go

parts.note: form is conventional behaviour, as in bad form

indicators.note: head to go says the first letter of the helping word is dropped

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A school's conduct means helping its principal to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean the act of setting something up or establishing it.

clue.text: Son upset about online animosity

indicators.note: about means turned round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: to upset is to tip over
E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A boy is distressed about something hostile said on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is ill will or malice, a form of hostility.

clue.text: Criminal letting go of guard

indicators.note: letting go of says those two letters are released from the word

parts.note: a criminal is an offender

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is released by a guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting go' takes the clue's own OF out of OFFENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a protective guard, such as a fireguard or a buffer on a boat.

clue.text: Risk having case overturned or extended

indicators.note: overturned completes the flip, so the last casing letter becomes the first one
having case points at the outer letters of the risk word, its casing, the first of which becomes the other

parts.note: danger is risk

explanation.surface: A legal hazard: a court verdict reversed, or lengthened.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the case of DANGER, its outer D and R, is turned over, giving R...D.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranged means roamed or stretched over an area, so it covered a distance.
